overlap.title: “shall devour the palaces” — the Greek has “shall devour the foundations” (Amos 1:4, 1:7, 1:10, 1:12, 1:14 and 2:5)
overlap.summary: In the refrain of Amos 1–2 the KJV has the fire “devour the palaces” of Hazael’s house, Gaza, Tyrus, Bozrah, Rabbah and Jerusalem. Brenton’s Greek prints θεμέλια at each of these verses, which Brenton’s own English renders “foundations”.
overlap.reasoning: At each verse the Hebrew quoted prints ארמנות (ארמנתיה, ארמנותיה) after the verb for devouring, and the KJV renders it “palaces”. The Greek prints θεμέλια, “foundations”, at the same place at each verse. A palace is a building and a foundation is the base of one; the two nouns name different things.
overlap.scope: T applies at Amos 1:4, Amos 1:7, Amos 1:10, Amos 1:12, Amos 1:14 and Amos 2:5. The record does not say what the Hebrew words quoted mean, and does not say which Greek word corresponds to which Hebrew word. This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. The English quoted from Brenton’s own page is given only to show how that edition renders the Greek it prints; it is not a lexicon entry. The same Greek noun is printed at all six verses; the record does not say how the Greek of other verses of Amos 1–2 compares. At 1:4 Brenton’s Greek prints υἱοῦ Ἄδερ where the KJV prints Benhadad; that is a difference of form in a name and is not the finding. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek quoted is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
overlap.decision: Distinct finding: ethical ritual comparison or Amos palace/foundation wording does not cover this Micah wording.
